Generation 1 settled the open questions and none of them beat this molecule. Every diazine lost to pyridine - pyrimidin-4-yl 0.44, pyrazin-2-yl 0.29, pyridazin-3-yl 0.25, pyrimidin-2-yl 0.23 against about 0.50 - so exactly one ring nitrogen, ortho to the donor, is the requirement and a second one costs more the closer it sits to the hinge. Every linker variant also lost but survived: sulfonyl 0.37, reversal 0.36, urea 0.37, thioamide 0.40. And a second ortho-nitrogen azine on the cap did not add. So activity is at its ceiling and the only gain left is drug-likeness. The cap is activity-neutral across ring sizes, which means I should pick it purely on SA - and cyclopropanecarboxamide measured SA 1.86 where this cyclobutyl version sits at 1.95. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 17 the cyclobutane CH, a non-ring bond, so I swap the four-membered ring for a three-membered one. Everything that carries activity is untouched. Expected product: about 288 Da, and if SA drops as it did before this should edge past 2.31.
